title: Recording: As Far As We Can Go by Ringo Starr | 1978
content:
Startling Studios, Ascot
Producers: Joe Walsh, Russ Ballard
Engineer: Jim Nipar

Ringo Starr recorded ‘As Far As We Can Go’ for his ninth studio album, Old Wave, on 23 July 1978.

The oldest recording on the album, the backing track was taped at Startling Studios in Starr’s Tittenhurst Park home. It was one of several songs recorded for an aborted album project produced by Russ Ballard, who also wrote the song.

Starr retained a liking for ‘As Far As We Can Go’, and played it to Joe Walsh and Jim Nipar to see if it would work on Old Wave. A new demo was recorded by Walsh and pianist Joe Vitale on 9 April 1982 at Santa Barbara Sound Recording. Walsh then brought the tape to Starr, but it was decided that Ballard’s version was superior.

The 24-track tape was sent to Walsh in LA to work on. Walsh removed the orchestra, and made another mix retaining the brass instruments, but he remained unhappy with the results.

Eventually, Walsh decided to scrap everything but Starr’s 1978 vocals. The song was edited from 5:32 to 3:52, removing a verse in the process. Vitale then added a new piano part on 11 August 1982, and Walsh overdubbed Mellotron and Prophet synthesizer parts.

It was tough, because the original Fender Rhodes piano was slightly out of time, so I couldn’t use it as a guide. I essentially played solely to Ringo’s vocal – that’s it. That was a tricky one!
Joe Vitale
